summary: Contestants prepare a resume, cover letter, and professional portfolio to demonstrate their skills and accomplishments. They participate in an advanced interview scenario and are evaluated on professionalism, portfolio quality, communication, and ethical workplace practices. The event includes both a technical submission and an in-person interview.
time_limits: No more than fifty (50) minutes for certification test
No more than fifteen (15) minutes for interview
submission_requirements: Submit one combined PDF file: Resume and Cover Letter
Contestant ID is required for all submissions
Materials must follow BPA Graphic Standards and proper use of BPA logo and/or organization’s name
Materials from non-registered contestants and/or those missing Contestant ID cannot be accepted
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
what_to_bring: Paper portfolio no larger than 8 1/2”x11” in plastic sheet protectors or electronic portfolios may be displayed on a notebook/laptop computer or tablet
One (1) copy of your resume and cover letter submitted at presentation check-in (both preliminaries and finals)
competencies: Create a tailored Applicant Tracking System (ATS) optimized résumé, cover letter, and a professional portfolio showcasing skills, accomplishments, and qualifications
Demonstrate strong employability and career advancement skills including adaptability, initiative, and continuous learning
Research career opportunities, industry trends, credentials, and expectations for professional image and branding
Communicate respectfully and ethically in diverse work environments, demonstrating integrity and effective collaboration with others
Exhibit advanced interview communication skills through persuasive storytelling, situational awareness, and confident interpersonal interaction
Demonstrate professionalism when discussing salary, benefits, and job offers
Use networking skills to build professional connections through career events, organizations, and personal interactions
Demonstrate advanced interviewing skills by giving clear, confident answers to interview and judge questions, and using examples to explain skills and experiences

rubric.criterion: Materials indicate contestant applied for one of the positions shown on the Organizational Chart of Digital Solutions found in the Style & Reference Manual.
Contestant submitted their Cover Letter and Resume in one (1) combined PDF file.

rubric.description: Engaging and specific, effectively captures attention.
All skills are clearly relevant to the position, well-explained, and directly applicable to the requirements.
Strong, compelling summary; leaves a memorable impression.
Well-organized, enhances readability and visual appeal.
Clearly listed at the top, prominently highlights target role.
Well-organized, enhances readability and visual appeal.
Completely in reverse chronological order, facilitating clear career progression.
Strong introduction; made a very positive first impression.
Positive, courteous, sincere, confident; good posture and eye contact.
Proper grammar and pronunciation; pleasant voice and tone.
Demonstrated strong job skills, good work habits, and problem-solving abilities.
Appropriate and informed answers; good knowledge of the position and company; demonstrated initiative and enthusiasm.
Expressed thanks and concluded the interview effectively.

judging_notes: Method of evaluation: judged
AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed

No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own mobile device only as a hotspot to access their digital portfolio. The device(s) must be set up prior to entering the presentation room
No time will be given for the setup of equipment and must be done solely by the contestant
Portfolio will not be submitted; the contestant will take the portfolio into the interview to be used to demonstrate job competence. Portfolios must not be left with judges
At NLC, contestants will take the Professional Communications certification exam. Contestants passing this certification will have 50 points added to their event score.
Pearson profile must be created at https://certiport.pearsonvue.com before attending NLC
Contestants must include their BPA Contestant ID in their Pearson profile when they register
Certiport Parent/Legal Guardian Consent Form must be uploaded to: education@bpa.org
Reference materials are not allowed for certification testing
No more than fifty (50) minutes for certification test
Length of event: no more than fifteen (15) minutes for interview
Finals may be part of the competition
Business cards, thank you notes, etc. are not permitted

Contestant will indicate on his/her resume the position for which he/she is applying. There are openings in all departments of Digital Solutions shown on the Organizational Chart found in the Style & Reference Manual
Resume work/volunteer history must be in reverse chronological order
Contestant may interview for any position listed on the organizational chart for which he/she is qualified
Contestants that do not apply for a position for one of these positions will be disqualified

Information in the cover letter and resume must be authentic; however, contestants may choose to use a fictitious personal address and telephone number. The use of references on the resume is optional.
The cover letter must be addressed as follows: Ms. Julie Smith, Manager, Human Resources Department, Digital Solutions, 1365 King Avenue, Columbus, OH 43212

This is a pre-submitted event. Regional and state conferences have specific deadlines prior to the national deadlines. Please consult the regional or state conference administrator for those deadlines. For the National Leadership Conference, submit project files at https://upload.bpa.org no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on April 1, 2027.

An auto-generated confirmation will be provided upon project submission for the National Leadership Conference; individual confirmation cannot be provided. No changes can be made to the project after the date of submission.
Contestant ID is required for all submissions. Materials from non-registered contestants and/or those missing Contestant ID cannot be accepted.
Materials must follow the organization’s BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name. Refer to the BPA Graphic Standards in the Style & Reference Manual.
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level. Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC.
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged event.
Contestants may not enter both Interview Skills and Advanced Interview Skills in the same year.
Advanced Interview Skills may be repeated.
Contestants must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked.
